title: Coding Agents vs Classical TAMP Planners

beats.text: Can an autonomous coding agent outplan classical robotics engines across complex, multi-object task and motion environments?
beats.visual_focus: Dual chalkboard split showing robotic arm motion trajectory versus synthesized Python policy code blocks.

beats.text: Classical TAMP couples discrete search with continuous kinematic constraints, suffering exponential search explosion as object count N scales.
beats.visual_focus: Exponential branching tree labeled O(b^N) colliding with geometric boundary collision hulls.

beats.text: Instead of solving per instance, frontier models like Claude Code synthesize generalized algorithmic policy scripts in simulator sandboxes.
beats.visual_focus: Simulator-in-the-loop feedback graph: LLM agent emits policy code, executes in KinDER simulator, inspects runtime traces.

beats.text: Agents iteratively test edge cases, calibrate physics models, and freeze verified programs for instant execution on held-out worlds.
beats.visual_focus: Algorithmic synthesis loop: program generation mapped to verified test suite pass rate with frozen policy deployment.

beats.text: Across ninety-eight thousand test episodes, synthesized code achieved ninety-five percent success, beating hand-crafted planners with ten-fold less computation.
beats.visual_focus: Bar chart comparing 47% classical planner success vs 95% agent success alongside a 10x compute reduction badge.
